paragraphs.source_en: Well, well! This affair too, it turns out, was a plot. Indeed, the power of businessmen is a formidable thing. To send my master, who is already as gaunt as a coal cinder, into a fit of excitement; to make his head, from sheer anguish, a slippery perilous place where even flies may skid; to cause that head to fall into the same fate as Aeschylus: all this is the power of businessmen. What force makes the earth revolve about its axis, I do not know. But what moves the whole of society is, beyond all doubt, money. Those who understand the power of this money and can freely bring its majesty into play are none other than the gentlemen of business. That the sun rises safely in the east and sets safely in the west is also entirely thanks to businessmen. Until now I have been kept in the household of an uncomprehending poor scholar, and failed to know the blessings of businessmen; that was truly careless of me. On this point, even my benighted and obstinate master will probably have no choice but to awaken somewhat this time. If he persists to the end in his stubborn notion, the matter will be dangerous indeed. My master’s most precious life may no longer be secure; I do not know what he will say after meeting Suzuki, and just how far he has awakened will only become clear from the circumstances of their meeting. At this point I cannot dawdle for even a moment. Though I am only a cat, since it concerns my master’s fate, naturally I cannot be easy. I hurriedly slipped past Mr. Suzuki and returned home ahead of him.
